title: Microshard coalescing and decode-pacing scheduler for paged-attention KV pools
creator: Priya Patel
description: Reduce tail latency and memory fragmentation in the paged KV cache by coalescing small microshards, introducing an allocation frontier, and implementing a decode-pacing scheduler that coordinates prefill and finalize phases across kernels. Goal is to improve 95th/99th token latency under mixed workload while keeping steady-state memory overhead within current targets.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-token latency reduced by >= 18% on the mixed-chat benchmark for 1K concurrent sessions
KV cache fragmentation metric (free-run fragments per GB) reduced by >= 35% after 24h of churn
No regression (>3%) in median per-token throughput for long-context (>8k) workloads
Automated canary runs and rollout policy integrated into console (canary->ramp->global)
Unit and integration tests covering microshard coalescing, allocation frontier, and decode-pacing logic merged
implementation_notes: Introduce a microshard abstraction: sub-64KB KV segments that can be merged when adjacent and lightly-used
Allocation frontier: maintain per-shard high-water timestamp plus eviction-priority score (age + reuse-prob) to drive coalesce vs evict decisions
Decode-pacing scheduler: token decode work is throttled by a per-GPU token budget that favors prefill paths with warm KV hints; uses async priority queues to avoid head-of-line blocking
Kernel hint map: expose lightweight hints to kernel selection (dense vs sparse attention) based on contiguous microshard runs and sequence-length histogram within request
Backpressure: when coalescing is in progress, temporarily favor small decode batches and route large batched prefill to spare capacity tier to avoid latency cliffs
Metrics: add kv.microshard_count, kv.coalesce_ops, scheduler.pacing_slack, kv.fragmentation_ratio to telemetry; dashboards in runtime-ops
decisions: Do microshard coalescing in the allocation path instead of background compaction to limit IO spikes (chosen after perf testing)
Prefer soft coalescing thresholds (usage < 5% for 30m) to avoid oscillation in high-churn customers
Scheduler initially implemented in userspace coordinator with future plan to push critical hot-path checks into runtime C++ for lower latency
Kernel hinting implemented via a compact 16-bit tag per request route to avoid metadata bloat
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed. Microshard abstraction prototype shows 20% reduction in measurable fragmentation on synthetic churn traces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1247)
2026-02-25: Benchmarked decode-pacing alg with mixed chat and embedding traffic. Identified worst-case pacing_slack under 95th percentile; tuned budget constants
2026-03-02: Implemented allocation frontier and integrated the eviction-priority score into the page allocator. Noted CPU overhead ~2% on an 8xA100 instance during aggressive coalesce — optimizing
2026-03-09: Added initial kernel-hint map and routing in runtime. End-to-end canary begun for small internal service (canary-2). Observed 12% 95th latency improvement for canary-2
2026-03-13: Code review feedback addressed; moving scheduler hot-loop to C++ shim to shave lock contention (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1283)
reviews: Design review 2026-02-18: feedback to avoid synchronous coalesce during peak; agreed to use cooperative coalesce tokens (Lead: Mateo Rivera)
Security review 2026-03-04: no new data flows; reviewed by Security (Anjali Rao). KMS/HSM unaffected
Perf review 2026-03-10: baseline and canary results reviewed; recommended adding a rig to simulate multi-tenant noisy neighbors
qa_plan: Unit tests for coalesce/undo operations and allocation frontier scoring
Deterministic integration test that simulates 48h of churn and validates fragmentation_ratio
Canary rollout with staged traffic: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on latency regressed >5%
Chaos scenario: inject node OOM and ensure scheduler routes prefill to spare tier without losing >2% success rate
risk_mitigation: CPU overhead from coalescing: limit coalesce work per-second and add dynamic backoff based on node load
Oscillation in coalesce/evict: implement hysteresis with time windows and exponential backoff
Long rollout: add feature flag to gate decode-pacing and ability to disable per-customer via Console
Observability gaps: pre-merge ensure all new metrics have alerts and dashboards
